title: On the Mysteries (Taylor Translation)
author: Iamblichus
description: On the Mysteries of the Egyptians, Chaldeans and Assyrians by Iamblichus, in the English translation by Thomas Taylor (1758-1835), the 'English Platonist' whose renderings brought Neoplatonism to the Romantics and later to Theosophy (first published 1821). It is the same treatise as De Mysteriis: Iamblichus, writing as the Egyptian priest Abamon, answers Porphyry's objections to ritual by defending theurgy as the means of the soul's union with the gods. Topics include the classes of divine beings (gods, archangels, angels, daemons, heroes and souls) and how to recognise their epiphanies, the meaning of sacrifice and prayer, divination by dreams, oracles and inspiration, Egyptian symbolic theology, and fate and providence. Taylor's notes connect the work to Proclus and the wider Platonic tradition. This version is historically important for the English-speaking esoteric revival.
editionNote: Curator-supplied PDF and EPUB from the organised ebook collection.
rights: Thomas Taylor's translation was published in 1821; public domain in the USA as a pre-1929 publication. Rights can vary by country.
